prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Labour’s 2005 manifesto sets a single aim: government should deliver opportunity and security for all in a changing world. Building on stability since 1997, it pledges a third term of reform grounded in rights and responsibilities, high employment, world‑class public services, safer communities, and active global leadership.

Record since 1997
- Economy: Lowest inflation for decades; 2m more in work; low interest rates; rising incomes; 300k more businesses; fewer children and pensioners in absolute poverty.
- Public services: Major investment; more teachers, nurses and doctors; primary school results up; heart/cancer deaths down.
- Welfare and work: New Deal cut long‑term youth unemployment; pensioners and families better off.
- Crime: Overall crime down 30%; more police and community support officers; faster justice.
- Global: Leading in an enlarged EU; aid more than doubled; UK pioneered emissions trading.

Key commitments
- Economy and jobs: Keep low debt, 2% inflation target, fiscal rules; no rise in basic/top income tax; targeted help for families and business; aim for 80% employment; raise minimum wage; reform incapacity benefits; boost skills, science and R&D (to 2.5% of GDP by 2014); smart regulation; strong competition; modern planning; major transport investment (rail upgrades, bus concessions, road pricing debate).
- Education: Personalised learning; more parental engagement; primary literacy/numeracy push; all secondary schools to be independent specialist schools; at least 200 Academies by 2010; stronger discipline; high‑quality vocational routes and apprenticeships; EMAs; FE reform; universities to expand with variable fees capped at £3,000, more grants/bursaries, and extra science funding.
- NHS and public health: Free, universal care; maximum 18 weeks from GP referral to treatment by 2008; real patient choice; more primary/community services and modern community hospitals; use independent/voluntary providers to add capacity; tougher action on MRSA; less bureaucracy; stronger clinical governance; expand dentistry; integrate health and social care; healthier diets in schools; clearer food labelling; tighter junk‑food marketing; phased smoking restrictions; health trainers to cut inequalities.
- Crime, ASB and borders: Neighbourhood policing team in every community; 24,000 CSOs; tougher powers on antisocial behaviour and alcohol disorder; more drugs testing/treatment; Serious Organised Crime Agency; tighter controls on knives/guns; reduce reoffending; stronger victims’ rights. Points‑based immigration; employer penalties for illegal working; biometric visas/ePassports; voluntary ID cards linked to passports; faster, firmer asylum system; robust counter‑terror powers alongside prosecutions.
- Families, older people, housing: Halve child poverty by 2010; expand Sure Start to every community; 15 free nursery hours (moving to 20); extended schools 8am–6pm; more childcare help; paid maternity leave to 9 months (aim 12); extend flexible working; pension credit uprated with earnings to 2007–08; long‑term pensions consensus; flexible retirement; individual care budgets; raise homeownership (higher stamp duty threshold); more and better social housing, choice‑based lettings.
- Environment and international: Lead on climate change (–20% CO2 by 2010; –60% by 2050), renewables and efficiency; Marine Act; fair trade and CAP reform; 0.7% aid by 2013; debt relief; universal access to basic health/education and AIDS treatment; active EU role (referendum on Constitutional Treaty), NATO at core of defence; modern armed forces and retain nuclear deterrent; UN reform.
- Quality of life and culture: Free national museums; wider participation (Creative Sparks); community sport facilities, more school PE/competitive sport; 2012 Olympics legacy; BBC governance reform; digital switchover 2008–2012; stronger IP; modern libraries; cleaner neighbourhoods and higher recycling.
- Democracy and equality: More local/neighbourhood power; support social enterprise and youth volunteering; stronger, freer local government; council tax kept under control; further devolution (Wales/London/regions); restore NI devolution with end to paramilitarism; complete Lords reform; Single Equality Act; new Commission for Equality and Human Rights; stronger protections against hate while upholding free speech.
</text>
